Lecture Notes: Memory Structures for Embodied Agents
1. Three Kinds of Memory
Episodic memory stores what happened and when. Semantic memory stores what is true regardless of when it was learned. Procedural memory stores how to act.
Memory type	Typical store	Example
episodic	event log	the cup was on the left shelf at 10:02
semantic	knowledge graph	cups are kept in the kitchen
procedural	policy	open the drawer before reaching in
2. Benchmarks
We compare agents on 4 benchmark suites: HomeTidy, ShelfQA, DoorNav and ToolUse-12 (all fictional, invented for these notes).
Suite	Episodes	Best success rate
HomeTidy	1,200	64.5%
ShelfQA	800	71.2%
DoorNav	2,000	88.0%
ToolUse-12	600	42.7%
3. Open Problems
- When should an agent forget?
- How to merge episodic traces into semantic facts
- Evaluating memory without leaking test episodes
Synthetic lecture notes for evaluation only.
